text:
incbot: Paging: Elevated 5xx and gateway timeouts for customer Orchid Labs on dedicated cluster eu-west-2d. Impacting ~15% of requests. Alert rule: dedicated.customer.errors > 10% for 5m :rotating_light:

ryan_oncall: on it — I'll triage. Can someone drop recent logs and the node list for that cluster?

maria_sre: pulling metrics now. Error mix: 502/504 from gateway + 500s from model workers. Latency p50 -> 120ms, p95 -> 4.8s. Token throughput down ~30%.

ian_ops: looks like GPU utilization on pool orchid-eu-2 is pegged at 98% on 3 nodes, others at 40-60%. KV cache eviction rate spiked at 21k/s. Possible noisy neighbor or long KV-hot sessions.

lucy_runtime: confirming—KV cache misses for Orchid Labs model variant v1.3 jumped. Some workers showing OOM logs and retry loops. Posting grep of recent worker errors:

```
[2026-03-15T18:12:03Z] worker-13 ERROR Runtime: kv_cache_miss for key session:orchid-abc123 size=272MB
[2026-03-15T18:12:04Z] worker-13 ERROR Runtime: allocating tensor failed: cuda out of memory
[2026-03-15T18:12:04Z] worker-13 ERROR Inference: 500 InternalError: model exec failure
```

ashley_se: @orchid-eng are you running any long-running interactive sessions or heavy batch jobs?

orchid-eng: We have a fine-tuned retriever pipeline that kicks off occasional long-prefix inferences for nightly indexing, but shouldn't be heavy right now. We're seeing failed user requests though. Not intentionally running anything heavy.

josh_support: Customer-reported errors started ~18:10Z. We have several open tickets; SLA impact: some customers seeing 5xx on key API routes.

ryan_oncall: immediate mitigation plan: 1) throttle Orchid Labs traffic at the gateway to reduce sustained pressure 2) enable temporary routing to fallback pool (orchid-eu-standby) with smaller model variant 3) bump reserved workers by +2 on pool if capacity allows 4) evict suspected noisy sessions and clear KV cache prefix for Orchid.

maria_sre: running throttle now: `curl -X POST https://api.redwood/route/throttle -d '{"route":"orchid-api","rate":0.7}'` -> applied. Observability: error rate dipped to 11% -> 9% in the first 30s.

ian_ops: attempting to scale reserved workers: `infractl pools scale --pool orchid-eu-2 --delta 2` -> API returned partial success: 1 node added, second failed due to AZ capacity.

lucy_runtime: enabling fallback routing to standby pool for new requests only. Added policy: prefer orchard-eu-standby, model variant v1.2-quant. NOTE: quality delta might exist, advising CS to warn customers.

ashley_se: applied KV prefix purge for Orchid sessions: `runtimectl kv purge --prefix orchid/session/ --confirm`. Post-purge evictions tracked. Watch for regens.

josh_support: telling customers about transient degradation and fallback. Drafting message: "We're routing new requests to a standby pool to restore availability; some requests may see slightly different responses."

ryan_oncall: logs after mitigation (18:18Z): gateway 5xx rate down to 6%, latency p95 down to 1.2s, GPU util drop to ~72% on the main pool. Still seeing intermittent 500s on a couple workers.

maria_sre: temporary improvement looks good. Need to identify root cause: noisy neighbor or memory leak. Snapshotting worker heap and nvml stats for the problematic nodes.

ian_ops: capturing node attachments: `kubectl get pods -n orchid --selector=pool=orchid-eu-2 -o wide` -> nodes worker-12,13,14. Worker-13 had repeated OOMs. I'm cordoning worker-13 and draining: `kubectl drain worker-13 --ignore-daemonsets`

lucy_runtime: while draining, create policy to reject long prefix sessions over 15s and route them to batch executor. Applying rule.

ashley_se: summary for handoff to night oncall: - Incident: elevated 5xx/timeouts for Orchid Labs on dedicated eu-west-2d cluster triggered by sustained KV hot sessions and GPU exhaustion on worker-13. - Mitigations applied: throttle route (0.7), fallback routing to orchid-eu-standby with v1.2-quant, kv prefix purge, cordon+drain worker-13, scale attempt +1 node. - Customer impact: ~15% failure at peak, now reduced to ~4-6% for last 10m. Some requests still hitting the drained worker for in-flight sessions — monitoring. - Next steps: investigate long-term mitigation (request quota for heavy jobs, autoscale policy review, KV cache LRU improvements), postmortem to include freq of long-prefix jobs.

josh_support: sent customer-facing note and flagged for follow-up. Customer asked for root cause timeline; requesting a write-up.

orchid-eng: appreciate quick triage. Please keep standby route in place until we confirm no further errors. We'll also audit any background indexing jobs.

ryan_oncall: acknowledged. Leaving the fallback route and throttle in place for now. Assigning follow-up owners: lucy_runtime -> root cause traces and heap analysis; maria_sre -> metrics + alert tuning; ian_ops -> autoscale + infra quota check; ashley_se -> customer comms & postmortem draft.

incbot: Incident acknowledged by oncall. Severity: Sev2. Labels: dedicated, noisy-neighbor-suspected, kv-eviction, gpu-exhaustion.

maria_sre: quick note — adding retrospective tasks to tracker: adjust dedicated capacity headroom for large tenants, add alert for kv_eviction_rate > 10k/s, add canary for reserved pool scale failures.

ryan_oncall: handing off to night oncall @maria_sre. If error rate creeps above 10% again, escalate to ENG-runtime immediately.

maria_sre: taking handoff. Monitoring dashboards and logs.

josh_support: closing incident channel for now; will reopen if regression. :white_check_mark:
